js_int_lesson_1:slide:0.title: ES6+ Modern Syntax 🚀
js_int_lesson_1:slide:0.content:
Key ES6+ features:
• Destructuring
• Spread operator
• Rest parameters
• Default parameters
• Template literals

js_int_lesson_1:slide:1.title: Destructuring
js_int_lesson_1:slide:1.content: Extract values from arrays and objects.

js_int_lesson_1:slide:2.title: Template Literals 📝
js_int_lesson_1:slide:2.content:
Powerful string formatting:
• Use backticks ` instead of quotes
• Embed expressions with ${}
• Multi-line strings built-in
• Tagged templates for custom processing

js_int_lesson_1:slide:3.title: Default Parameters 🎯
js_int_lesson_1:slide:3.content:
Set default values for function parameters:
• Defaults used when argument is undefined
• Can use expressions as defaults
• Earlier params available in later defaults

js_int_lesson_1:slide:4.title: Enhanced Object Literals ⚡
js_int_lesson_1:slide:4.content:
Shorter syntax for objects:
• Property shorthand
• Method shorthand
• Computed property names

js_int_lesson_1:question:0.explanation: Array destructuring assigns array elements to variables.

js_int_lesson_1:question:1.prompt: Which syntax is correct for template literals?
js_int_lesson_1:question:1.explanation: Template literals use backticks ` and ${} for interpolation.

js_int_lesson_1:question:2.prompt: What happens when you call greet() with function greet(name = "World")?
js_int_lesson_1:question:2.explanation: Default parameters are used when arguments are undefined or not provided.

js_int_lesson_1:question:3.prompt: What is { name, age } shorthand for?
js_int_lesson_1:question:3.explanation: Property shorthand creates properties with variable names and values.

js_int_lesson_2:slide:0.title: Spread Operator ... 📤
js_int_lesson_2:slide:0.content:
Spread expands elements:
• Combine arrays
• Clone objects
• Pass arguments

js_int_lesson_2:slide:2.title: Object Spread Deep Dive 🔄
js_int_lesson_2:slide:2.content:
Object spread for immutable updates:
• Clone objects without mutation
• Override specific properties
• Merge multiple objects
• Order matters for overrides!

js_int_lesson_2:slide:3.title: Rest Parameters in Functions 📥
js_int_lesson_2:slide:3.content:
Collect remaining arguments:
• Must be last parameter
• Creates a real array (not arguments object)
• Works with destructuring

js_int_lesson_2:slide:4.title: Spread vs Rest Comparison 🎯
js_int_lesson_2:slide:4.content:
Same syntax, different contexts:
• Spread: Expands (unpacks)
• Rest: Collects (packs)
• Position determines behavior

js_int_lesson_2:question:0.explanation: Rest (...args) collects remaining arguments into array.

js_int_lesson_2:question:1.prompt: What does { ...obj1, ...obj2 } produce if both have property "x"?
js_int_lesson_2:question:1.explanation: In object spread, later properties override earlier ones.

js_int_lesson_2:question:2.prompt: Where must rest parameter appear in function signature?
js_int_lesson_2:question:2.explanation: Rest parameter must be the last parameter in a function.

js_int_lesson_2:question:3.prompt: What does const [a, ...b] = [1, 2, 3] assign to b?
js_int_lesson_2:question:3.explanation: Rest in destructuring collects remaining elements into an array.

js_int_lesson_2:question:4.explanation: Each lesson objective is to build practical skill with one focused concept.

js_int_lesson_3:slide:0.title: Functional Array Methods 🔧
js_int_lesson_3:slide:0.content:
Transform arrays without mutation:
• **map**: Transform each element
• **filter**: Keep matching elements
• **reduce**: Combine to single value
• **find**: Get first match

js_int_lesson_3:slide:2.title: find() and findIndex() 🔍
js_int_lesson_3:slide:2.content:
Search for single elements:
• find(): Returns first matching element
• findIndex(): Returns index of first match
• Returns undefined/-1 if not found
• Stops searching after first match

js_int_lesson_3:slide:3.title: some() and every() ✅
js_int_lesson_3:slide:3.content:
Test array conditions:
• some(): At least one matches (OR)
• every(): All must match (AND)
• Return boolean values
• Short-circuit when result is determined

js_int_lesson_3:slide:4.title: includes() and flat() 📋
js_int_lesson_3:slide:4.content:
More useful array methods:
• includes(): Check if element exists
• flat(): Flatten nested arrays
• flatMap(): Map then flatten

js_int_lesson_3:question:0.explanation: filter() returns new array with elements passing the test.

js_int_lesson_3:question:1.prompt: What does find() return if no element matches?
js_int_lesson_3:question:1.explanation: find() returns undefined when no element satisfies the condition.

js_int_lesson_3:question:2.explanation: some() returns true because at least one element (3) is greater than 2.

js_int_lesson_3:question:3.explanation: every() returns true because all elements are greater than 0.

js_int_lesson_4:slide:0.title: Promises ⏳
js_int_lesson_4:slide:0.content:
A Promise represents future value.

States:
• **pending**: Initial
• **fulfilled**: Success
• **rejected**: Error

js_int_lesson_4:slide:2.title: Promise.all() - Parallel Execution 🚀
js_int_lesson_4:slide:2.content:
Run multiple promises in parallel:
• All must succeed for success
• Fails fast on first rejection
• Results in same order as input
• Great for independent async tasks

js_int_lesson_4:slide:3.title: Promise Error Handling 🛡️
js_int_lesson_4:slide:3.content:
Proper error handling strategies:
• .catch() for chain errors
• reject() for explicit failures
• Error propagation through chain
• finally() for cleanup

js_int_lesson_4:slide:4.title: Promise.allSettled() & Promise.race() 🏁
js_int_lesson_4:slide:4.content:
More Promise combinators:
• allSettled(): Wait for all, never rejects
• race(): First to settle wins
• any(): First to fulfill wins

js_int_lesson_4:question:1.prompt: What happens if one promise in Promise.all() rejects?
js_int_lesson_4:question:1.explanation: Promise.all() fails fast - it rejects immediately when any promise rejects.

js_int_lesson_4:question:2.explanation: finally() always executes after the promise settles, regardless of outcome.

js_int_lesson_4:question:3.prompt: Which method waits for all promises and never rejects?
js_int_lesson_4:question:3.explanation: Promise.allSettled() waits for all promises and returns their results, never rejects.

js_int_lesson_4:question:4.prompt: What is the main objective of "Promises Deep Dive"?
js_int_lesson_4:question:4.explanation: Each lesson objective is to build practical skill with one focused concept.

js_int_lesson_5:slide:0.title: Async/Await ✨
js_int_lesson_5:slide:0.content:
Write async code like sync:
• **async**: Makes function return Promise
• **await**: Pauses until Promise resolves
• Use try/catch for errors

js_int_lesson_5:slide:2.title: Try/Catch Error Handling 🛡️
js_int_lesson_5:slide:2.content:
Proper error handling with async/await:
• Wrap await calls in try/catch
• Catch specific error types
• Always handle errors gracefully
• Can re-throw for higher-level handling

js_int_lesson_5:slide:3.title: Parallel Await with Promise.all 🚀
js_int_lesson_5:slide:3.content:
Run async operations in parallel:
• Sequential await is slow
• Promise.all() runs in parallel
• Use when requests are independent
• Significant performance improvement

js_int_lesson_5:slide:4.title: Advanced Async Patterns 🎯
js_int_lesson_5:slide:4.content:
Common async patterns:
• Async loops (for...of with await)
• Retry logic
• Timeout handling
• Async IIFE

js_int_lesson_5:question:0.explanation: await can only be used inside async functions.

js_int_lesson_5:question:1.prompt: What is the benefit of using try/catch with async/await?
js_int_lesson_5:question:1.explanation: try/catch provides clean, synchronous-style error handling for async code.

js_int_lesson_5:question:2.prompt: How do you run multiple awaits in parallel?
js_int_lesson_5:question:2.explanation: Promise.all() runs multiple promises in parallel and awaits all results.

js_int_lesson_5:question:3.prompt: What does an async function always return?
js_int_lesson_5:question:3.explanation: Async functions always return a Promise, even if you return a plain value.

js_int_lesson_5:question:4.explanation: Each lesson objective is to build practical skill with one focused concept.
